Let $A$ be the event that the product of the obtained numbers is $12,$ and let $B$ be the event that the product of the obtained numbers is $18.$ Then the probability that the product is $12$ or $18$ is given by $P(A\cup B).$

Since the product has a single value, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, i.e., $P(A\cap B)=0.$

We can find $P(A)$ and $P(B)$ by computing the necessary ratios. The product could be anything between $1$ and $64,$ and there are $8\cdot 8=64$ possible outcomes. 

A product of $12$ could be formed in the following $4$ ways:

$$
{(2,6),(6,2),(3,4),(4,3)}.
$$

A product of $18$ could be formed in the following $2$ ways:

$$
{(3,6),(6,3)}.
$$

Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{4}{64}, \\ P(B) & =\frac{2}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\  & =\frac{4}{64}+\frac{2}{64}-0 \\  & =\frac{6}{64} \\  & =\frac{3}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$
